\[
b^2-(2b+3)=(b-3)(b+1)=p^n,\quad p\text{ prime}, n\ge 2.
\]

Since \(\gcd(b-3,b+1)=\gcd(b-3,4)\).

- If \(p\) is odd, the factors are coprime, so one is \(1\) and the other is \(p^n\), giving difference \(4\), so \(p^n=5\), impossible for \(n\ge 2\).
- If \(p=2\), write
\[
b-3=2^u,\quad b+1=2^v,\quad v>u.
\]
Then
\[
4=2^v-2^u=2^u(2^{v-u}-1).
\]
Thus \(2^{v-u}-1=1\), so \(v-u=1\), and \(2^u=4\), giving \(u=2,v=3\). Hence
\[
b-3=4 \implies b=7.
\]

Check: \(100_7-23_7=49-(14+3)=32=2^5\), a good number.

\[
\boxed{7}
\]
